scenes.name: Talking Heads
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Estudiantes de la Escuela de Diseño de Rhode Island que no querían ser llamados art rock: imagen «normal» y pulcra frente al cuero del CBGB, guitarra «finita, limpia y metálica» de David Byrne, el bajo melódico de Tina Weymouth con slap a lo Larry Graham y Jerry Harrison (ex Modern Lovers) a los teclados. Con «Psycho Killer» fundan los nervios de la new wave, pero siempre con funk, tocado como blancos de clase media. Brian Eno, casi un quinto miembro y su George Martin, produce una trilogía de «funk psicodélico» inspirada en Parliament-Funkadelic: More Songs About Buildings and Food («Take Me to the River»), Fear of Music (la desorientación de 1979, «Life During Wartime», «I Zimbra» con un poema de Hugo Ball) y Remain in Light (1980), afrofunk construido con improvisaciones recortadas en el estudio, polirritmo y predicadores radiofónicos: «una obra maestra». Las tensiones por la autoría con Eno llevan a un regreso al pop; Weymouth y Frantz triunfan con Tom Tom Club.

podcast.body: After his time with Talking Heads, Jerry Harrison engaged in independent solo musical endeavors. "Jerry Harrison does stuff on his own"

xref.title: Contribution to New Wave
xref.body: The Talking Heads, with former Modern Lovers keyboardist Jerry Harrison, became a major component of the American New Wave era. This demonstrates the later success of musicians who emerged from the less-known scene. "And both the talking heads and the cars would eventually become major components of the American New Wave era."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Projects
xref.body: Following their time with Talking Heads, the members pursued various projects: David Byrne embarked on a solo career, Jerry Harrison also engaged in solo work, and Chris Frantz and Tina Weymouth formed the group Tom Tom Club. "David Byrne has a solo career, Jerry Harrison does stuff on his own and Chris and Tina are the Tom Tom Fub."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Very First Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Success of Members
xref.body: Following the band's dissolution in 1974, two of its members went on to achieve greater success. Drummer David Robertson found work with another Boston group, The Cars. Keyboardist Jerry Harrison joined the new band The Talking Heads. Both The Cars and The Talking Heads would later become significant components of the American New Wave era. "However, two members of the band went on to bigger and better things. Drummer David Robertson found work with another Boston group called The Cars and Keyboard is Jerry Harrison soon hooked up with a new band called The Talking Heads."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
